Basis: the accepted DevMasters agency architecture. Admin and approved-Expert portals only. Company requests are public and account-free; experts work directly with the requesting company. No project tasks, timesheets or deliverable management.

READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION
All exact fields, lengths, defaults, enums and support tables are proposed v1 specifications. The source fixes the business model, not a deployed schema.
PK = primary key; FK = foreign key; UQ = single-column unique constraint. Multiple PK-marked identifiers in a bridge form one composite primary key.
Nullable = database-level nullability. Required-on-issue rules still apply to draft offer fields. “None” means no default; it does not mean an optional field.
All timestamps are proposed as timestamptz(3); dates remain date. UUID identity and integer record_version are proposals. Apply updated_at and record_version changes in every write path.
Default FK actions: RESTRICT on delete/update. Preserve history by disabling or archiving records. Retention durations, legal policy wording and controlled purging remain unresolved.
IMPORTANT: accepted offer ≠ selected expert. Selection must reference the exact valid acceptance. Issued terms and file-version references are preserved.
This package is documentation, not an executed migration. Planned tests have not been run against an application or database.
Tables: All exact table/field definitions are proposed physical design. 'Core ER entity' means the entity exists in the accepted architecture, not that these columns were already approved.

Named groups of staff or expert permissions.
Atomic actions checked by backend authorization.
Rotate atomically, reject revoked/expired sessions and revoke the family on token reuse. Verification codes and short-lived recovery state remain in Redis, not business tables.
Verified internal company records; not login accounts.
Do not enforce unique company names: unrelated organizations may share a name. Linking never overwrites the original request submission.

At least one of email or phone must be present; contact.organization_id must agree with a linked request.organization_id.
Anonymous Invite Us to Bid and Hire Our Team submissions and agency follow-up.

Roles/headcount needed under one company request.
A request may initially have no structured roles. Headcount checks apply when offers reference a role; unstructured requests have no implied headcount cap.
Append-only agency notes and request activity history.
Staff-only. Public submissions cannot set arbitrary internal activity types or actor IDs.
Public application and, after approval, the expert profile.

Explicit refinement of the source ERD: user_id is nullable to store anonymous pre-approval applications. Review snapshots preserve later corrections. Approved does not automatically mean authenticated or active.
Immutable application review decisions and reviewed evidence.
Public corrections require a scoped, expiring correction token; they do not grant general portal access. File references must be validated when the review is recorded.
Controlled skill catalogue used for manual matching.
Mutable profile association; edits/removals are audited. created_at records initial association time; no business-history records cascade from this bridge.
Expert availability intervals for manual staff search.
Proposed rule: do not allow overlapping availability intervals for the same expert. Staff may correct intervals with audit history; no time tracking is introduced.
Append-only expert consent and withdrawal events.
Latest event per purpose determines operational consent. Retention periods and policy/legal wording are not supplied by the architecture; this is not a compliance determination.
One manual shortlist record per expert per request.
UNIQUE(request_id, expert_profile_id). Offers can address multiple roles from this one shortlist entry. Reject new shortlist entries for unapproved or suspended experts.
Append-only history of staff contact with shortlisted experts.
Interest is not acceptance. An agreement must be recorded as an offer_response against the exact issued version.
One DevMasters-to-expert offer, distinct from final selection.

Create offer and version 1 in one transaction. request/expert/candidate/request_role identity is immutable after first issue. Multiple offers per request/expert are allowed; a new engagement cycle requires a new offer.
Versioned terms and operational state of one expert offer.

UNIQUE(offer_id, version_no). Only drafts can change terms or attachment membership. After issue, only lifecycle metadata can change. Starting a revision supersedes the old version and invalidates it for new responses; past responses remain.
Immutable expert response to an exact issued offer version.

Many comments but at most one decision response per version. A new decision after changes/decline requires a new version. All acceptance channels satisfy current-version/expiry checks at recording; issued_at <= responded_at <= recorded_at. Late evidence is a comment, not backdated valid acceptance.
Append-only DevMasters selection decisions, separate from acceptance.

All decisions follow valid acceptance, matching the accepted workflow. Allow at most one SELECTED event per offer. A later NOT_SELECTED correction must cancel the existing placement atomically, not delete it. A new placement cycle requires a new offer.
Administrative record of a selected expert working directly with the company.
No tasks, timesheets, deliverables or project milestones. Negotiated material changes require a fresh accepted offer cycle; do not silently rewrite the historic terms link.
Logical private document whose bytes are stored outside PostgreSQL.
No public object URLs or binary file content in this table. Expert/request link tables establish ownership for anonymous uploads.
Immutable object metadata and mutable scan outcome for one uploaded file version.

UNIQUE(document_id, version_no) and UNIQUE(bucket_name, object_key). Never replace bytes under an existing key. Only CLEAN versions may be downloaded, attached to issued offers or used as valid evidence. Scanner updates do not change file identity.
Expert-to-document ownership links for CVs and supporting certificates.

Current profile attachments may change with audit history. Issued offer attachments and response evidence retain exact versions independently. Sharing CVs must check the relevant consent and staff permission.
Internal request attachments received through public forms or staff.
Staff-only by default. An expert receives a file only when an authorized exact document version is attached to their own issued offer; a shortlist entry alone does not grant file access.
Exact attachment versions included with one offer version.
Membership, labels and order lock when the offer version is issued. Never resolve to the latest document version at acceptance or placement time.
User-facing in-app inbox; email delivery is tracked separately.
UNIQUE(recipient_user_id, outbox_event_id, notification_type). Anonymous acknowledgement emails do not require notification or user rows; they use outbox events and delivery attempts.
Durable committed events queued independently of business decisions.
Insert with the business record, audit and notifications in one transaction. Queue publication and consumption may repeat; handlers must be idempotent. PUBLISHED does not mean email delivered.
Per-recipient, per-channel external notification delivery attempts.

UNIQUE(outbox_event_id, delivery_key, attempt_no). Claim/retry under a lock. Reuse the notification rather than insert duplicates. Ambiguous provider failures may still cause duplicate email; exactly-once external delivery is not promised.
Append-only security and business change history.
Normal application users cannot update/delete events. Immutable actor IDs remain resolvable through disabled accounts; legal retention/purge procedures are separate from routine CRUD.
Structured skill requirements for manual role matching.
Explicit refinement; architecture names skills and request requirements but does not specify this join table. Matching remains manual.
Exact supporting files for an attributed off-portal expert response.
Append-only after response commit. Staff-only by default; exposing evidence requires a separate authorization decision. No unvalidated evidence URL substitutes for private-file access.
Service catalogue for public pages and request categorization.
No service names are invented or seeded by this deliverable; actual catalogue remains to be supplied.
A request may be uncategorized at intake. Preserve original form choices separately in submission_snapshot.
Editable public content without a company portal.
UNIQUE(slug, locale). Audit content changes; full editorial versioning is not added in this version.
UNIQUE(template_key, channel, locale, version_no). Store no Gmail/Plasgate credentials here. Only active published templates may be used for new delivery attempts.
Database/JWT/Gmail/Plasgate/storage credentials remain protected runtime secrets, never settings values. Currency allowlists, upload limits and retention policy values require explicit approval.
Durable command deduplication for public intake and authenticated writes.

UNIQUE(actor_scope, key_hash). Complete record in the same transaction as the business change; enforce authorization again on replay. Public scopes must be unguessable signed tokens, not only email or IP.
Asynchronous private exports of requests, offers and placements.
No new project-management module. Expert access to agency-wide exports is not granted. Exports remain private and follow document authorization rules.

Constraints: Integrity specifications, not executable migration SQL. Row-local CHECKs cannot validate another table's state; use the composite FKs and guarded transactions/triggers listed here. Parent minimum-child rules require additional enforcement.
user_roles / role_permissions / expert_skills / expert_documents / request_documents / offer_documents / request_role_skills / request_services / offer_response_evidence
Composite primary key on the two identifier columns shown as PK.
Junctions do not receive a redundant surrogate ID.
All single-column UQ markers in Columns are unique constraints. Nullable unique links allow multiple unlinked records.
Use explicit composite keys below in addition; keep UUID identity immutable.
company_requests(contact_id, organization_id) -> contacts(id, organization_id); UNIQUE contacts(id, organization_id). CHECK contact_id IS NULL OR organization_id IS NOT NULL.
Prevents a verified contact from a different organization being linked.
expert_offers(candidate_id, request_id, expert_profile_id) -> candidates(id, request_id, expert_profile_id); add matching parent UNIQUE.
Prevents mixing an unrelated shortlist, request or expert.
expert_offers(request_role_id, request_id) -> request_roles(id, request_id); add matching parent UNIQUE.
Optional role link, but if present it belongs to this request.
expert_offers(current_version_id, id) -> offer_versions(id, offer_id); UNIQUE offer_versions(id, offer_id).
The current version cannot belong to another offer; current_version_id is populated before transaction commit.
Decision terms belong to the offer being decided.
selection_decisions(accepted_response_id, offer_version_id) -> offer_responses(id, offer_version_id); add matching parent UNIQUE.
FK enforces version match; a guarded transaction/trigger verifies response_type = ACCEPTED.
(supersedes_decision_id, offer_id) -> selection_decisions(id, offer_id); add matching parent UNIQUE.
Decision 1 has no predecessor; every later decision references the latest predecessor with a lower decision_no. Prevent cycles and branching.
placements(offer_id, request_id, expert_profile_id) -> expert_offers(id, request_id, expert_profile_id); add matching parent UNIQUE.
Denormalized request/expert columns cannot drift away from the offer.
The accepted version must be a version of this placement offer.
The exact response must be ACCEPTED; a plain FK cannot enforce its enum value.
placements(selection_decision_id, offer_id, offer_version_id, accepted_response_id) -> selection_decisions(id, offer_id, offer_version_id, accepted_response_id); add matching parent UNIQUE.
Verifies the identical offer/version/response chain; also verify SELECTED outcome.
delivery_attempts(notification_id, outbox_event_id) -> notifications(id, outbox_event_id); add matching parent UNIQUE.
An attempt cannot be linked to a notification from another event; nullable for anonymous recipients.

Business Rules: Transaction and authorization rules supplement the relational constraints. Source-derived requirements and proposed boundary rules are explicitly identified.
Company submissions create company_requests, optional documents and an acknowledgement outbox event without creating users. Staff link CRM records later.

Capture application with nullable expert_profiles.user_id. Approval writes expert_reviews and profile state; activation then links/invites a user. Portal guard requires ACTIVE account + APPROVED application + ACTIVE network.
Use an expiring scoped Redis token to correct a pending application without full portal access. Original application_snapshot is immutable; review snapshots capture the state actually evaluated.
Only approved active experts may enter new shortlists. Interest or outreach alone never proves acceptance. Availability remains informational unless an explicit policy makes it a hard blocker.
Lock offer, verify record_version and current draft, validate required terms and CLEAN attachments. Freeze snapshot/hash and atomically write issue state, inbox notification, audit and outbox.

Create sequential version; supersede old current version and point current_version_id to the draft in the same transaction. Historical responses survive. Issue revised terms and obtain fresh acceptance. No revisions after a placement exists.

Lock offer and current version; verify actor/channel, eligibility, ISSUED state and now() < expires_at. Insert immutable response and audit, then change state. Off-portal evidence requires staff attribution and evidence_summary, plus exact file versions when available.

Expiry blocks new acceptance; it does not retroactively cancel an acceptance validly recorded before the deadline. Expiry worker must lock and skip ACCEPTED versions. Late off-portal claims cannot bypass expiry by backdating responded_at.

Lock company request, request role if any, then offer in a fixed order. Verify current ACCEPTED version/response and selection permission. Capacity counts non-CANCELLED placements for the role, not accepted offers. Write decision, placement, notification, audit and outbox atomically.

Do not overwrite decisions. Append a reasoned superseding decision; a SELECTED-to-NOT_SELECTED correction cancels the linked placement in the same transaction. One selected placement cycle per offer; a later new cycle gets a new offer.
Original submitted company/contact fields never change when staff links or edits organizations/contacts. Contact linkage must belong to linked organization. Preserve placement company_name_snapshot.

PostgreSQL stores private file metadata, not bytes. Route access through authenticated/scoped API authorization. Block non-CLEAN files. Request documents are staff-only unless exact versions are intentionally attached to an expert offer.

Create document + first version + owner link atomically. Quarantine uploads until scan is CLEAN. Never mutate existing object bytes; never purge a version referenced by issued terms, acceptance evidence or placement history through routine CRUD.

Outbox, inbox and business state commit together. Dispatcher leases and retries committed events. Consumers deduplicate by event/delivery key. Delivery failure never reverses acceptance/selection. Provider timeout may make delivery UNKNOWN; avoid promises of exactly-once email.

Public acknowledgement requires an outbox event and delivery_attempts, but no user/notification. Public-upload ownership is derived from the submitted request/application, not from created_by_user_id.

Every expert read/write checks ownership through profile -> offer -> version -> response/placement. Never trust client-supplied user IDs. Staff review, offer issue and final selection are separately permissioned. Internal notes, audit, delivery diagnostics and response evidence remain staff-only.

Use unique scoped command keys plus request hashes. Lock competing aggregates and use record_version comparison; stale edits return conflict. Retried acceptance/selection commands return the original committed result, not a second decision.

Default all documented foreign keys to ON DELETE RESTRICT / ON UPDATE RESTRICT. Disable/archive referenced users and business masters; never cascade away offers, acceptances or evidence. Security/consent/file retention durations need approved policy; controlled purging is a separate reviewed workflow.

Store password/refresh-token hashes only. JWT keys, provider credentials and storage/database secrets stay in protected runtime configuration. OTP and verification/recovery challenges remain expiring Redis state with attempt limits; no raw secret in logs/outbox.

Derive request/offer/placement summaries from normalized records; avoid independently editable counters. Export jobs are staff-scoped, reauthorized at execution/download and stored as private documents.

Use JSONB only for versioned snapshots, templating, settings, event payloads and validated filters. Store relationships in typed FKs/junctions. Audit/outbox/idempotency entity references are explicitly logical, not guaranteed relational FKs.

Use Prisma native mappings for PostgreSQL types. Implement required CHECKs, triggers, exclusion/composite constraints and any unsupported features through reviewed migrations. Test PostgreSQL enforcement, not only DTO validation.
